title: The Mature Bass Player's Guide Book: Lessons and Stories ebass guitar from a Decade of Tea
description: Am I too old to start playing bass guitar? Have I left it too late? Will I ever feel confident playing? The Mature Bass Player’s Guidebook was written around the questions mature bass players often quietly ask themselves. This is not a traditional bass guitar method book filled with endless scales, exercises and theory. Instead, James Eager draws on more than 20 years of teaching thousands of adult bass players to explore the doubts, frustrations, confidence and identity shifts that come with learning later in life. Along the way, you’ll meet bass guitar players in their 50s, 60s, 70s and even 80s who have faced many of the same questions: What if I am not naturally gifted? Why does progress sometimes feel so slow? When do I start to feel like a bass player? Why do mistakes knock my confidence so much? How do I keep going when I feel stuck or behind? Their stories show what learning bass guitar later in life really looks like. Not a race to catch up, but a journey shaped by persistence, confidence, enjoyment, community and the decision to keep growing. You’ll also discover practical ideas for practice, resilience, mistakes, performing, playing with other musicians and making bass guitar fit naturally into your life. Learning bass guitar later in life is not a race to catch up. It is a chance to keep growing, creating and becoming. This book will show you what that journey can look like. “It is never too late to do something you are passionate about! James’s book is the perfect guide to following your heart and passion.” Leland Sklar Legendary session bassist for Phil Collins, James Taylor, Toto, Jackson Browne, Carole King and hundreds more “More than learning bass, this book gives you encouragement, perspective and belief. It might just change your life.” Scott Devine

title: Big Book of Bass: Strategies for Catching Largemouth and Smallmouth (The Freshwater Angler
description: The bible of bass fishing Ounce for ounce, no North American gamefish offers more excitement for anglers than bass. Any angler who has landed a feisty, ferocious two-pounder after 30 minutes of play remains hooked for life. No wonder 19.5 million anglers regularly fish for bass in the U.S, Canada, and central America. Bass fishing is now so popular that bass-catching tournaments have become a leading spectator sport across the continent, with top bass fishermen rivaling NASCAR drivers in the loyalty of their followers. With this impressive collection of up-to-date information, novice as well as experienced anglers will learn everything they need to know to catch both largemouth and smallmouth bass. Readers will find in-depth coverage of bass biology and behavior, with clear, concise text and more than 1,000 step-by-step photos. And the book shows the very latest innovations in lures and tackle suitable for catching trophy bass.
